findings.element: card stack (white / blue / amber cards) vs the Oct–Dec timeline
findings.problem: Fails fixed requirement L1. The timeline rule (y≈433, in 1280×720 canvas px) runs straight through the amber back card (y 248–448) and under the blue card, and the Dec dot (x≈840) sits under the blue card's bottom-left corner. There is about -15 px of clearance instead of the required ≥12 pt (16 px). It reads as a layout collision, not an overlap by design.
findings.fix: Keep the stack where it is (front card x 817–1135, y 200–399; amber layer bottom y 448). Move the timeline group (rule, three dots, three labels) down 96 px: rule at y=528, dots centred on it (top y=520), labels top y=560. That leaves 72 px (54 pt) between the amber card bottom and the dot tops, and about 60 px between the labels and the footer wordmark (y≈645). Re-check after the headline fix below so the stack doesn't move into the headline.

findings.problem: Four of five content headlines end in a runt: slide 2 'all quarter', slide 3 'September', slide 4 '41 sites', slide 6 'by Q1'. Each is a greedy wrap, not a chosen break, and four of them in six slides make the deck look unset.
findings.fix:
Slide 2: break as 'Sensor uptime held
above 99% all quarter' (see the slide 2 finding for size). Slide 3: 'Monthly readings grew 2.4×
from July to September'. Slide 4: 'The network ran at 99.3% uptime
across 41 live sites'. Slide 6: widen the headline box to 760 px so 'Next: 20 more sites by Q1' sits on one line at 56 px (≈680 px wide), top unchanged at y≈120.

findings.element: column chart, source footnote and right-hand third of the slide
findings.problem: The headline claims 2.4×, but the chart only shows three values. The viewer has to divide 290 by 120 themselves. The plot uses only x 80–816, so the right third (x 816–1216) is trapped white space with a lone 18 px footnote floating at mid-height. The axis line starts at x=80, 16 px in from the 64 px margin every other element uses, and category tick marks add junk.
findings.fix: Widen the plot area to x 64–960 (axis line starts exactly at x=64, bars about 180 px wide). Delete the category tick marks. Add the claim to the chart: a 1 px dashed ink-40% line at the Jul value height running from the Jul bar to the Sep bar, and a '2.4×' label at 28 px/700 ink just right of the Sep bar, vertically centred between that line and the Sep bar top. Keep the exact footnote 'Source: synthetic dataset v1 (fictional)' beside the chart (C1) at x 992–1216, 18 px, wrapping to 2 lines, with its last baseline on the axis baseline.

findings.problem: The three stats sit on equal 384 px columns but have very different widths, so the gaps read 88 px (99.3% → 41) and 287 px (41 → 6 h). That looks like a hole where a fourth stat was removed. All three are blue at the same 96 px weight, so nothing dominates, and the lower 40% of the slide (y 430–640) is left-over space.
findings.fix: Make it asymmetric. Put 99.3% at x=64, top y=272, 96 px/800 blue, with 'uptime' 22 px below it and the amber marker rule (see the colour finding) under the label. Stack the other two in a right column at x=704: '41' at 56 px/700 ink, top y=272, label 'sites live' below; a 1 px ink-20% rule at y=392 from x 704 to 1216; '6 h' at 56 px/700 ink, top y=416, label 'median repair time' below. Use a non-breaking space in '6 h'.

findings.element: statement 'Sensor uptime held above 99% all quarter'
findings.problem: The statement slide is set at 56 px (title scale, not hero) and is all ink, so it reads as a content slide missing its content. On the three-second test, the eye goes to the headline and then to the blue footer wordmark, the only colour on the slide, rather than to '99%'.
findings.fix: Set the statement at the hero size, 88 px/800, -0.02 em, line-height 1.08, in two lines: 'Sensor uptime held / above 99% all quarter'. The block runs from x=64, top y=232. Set '99%' in brand blue #2E4BD8 and add the amber marker rule under it. Move the subline 'Across all 41 sites, from July to September.' to 32 px below the block (top ≈ y 458). Leave nothing else on the slide.

findings.problem: Cover the 'Northstar Demo' wordmark and slides 1–5 could belong to any company: navy title, then white slides with a 64 px left margin. The brand's card-stack motif, the only ownable element, appears once, at the very end.
findings.fix: Bookend the deck with the stack. On slide 1, place the same three-card stack, enlarged (cards 440×300, radius 24, offsets +24/+24 for blue and +48/+48 for amber), with the front white card at x=872, y=210, so the amber layer bleeds off the right edge. The front card holds '41 sites' at 56 px/800 blue and 'live in Q3' at 22 px ink. Give that front card the same Morph name as the slide 6 front card, so the closing card ('41 → 61', below) reads as the same object updated. Don't add the stack to slides 2–5.

findings.problem: The brief sets amber as the one highlight per slide, but here it marks nothing. It is a decorative bar on slide 1 and the back layer of the stack on slide 6. Blue does all the highlighting (Sep bar, stats, North row, 20 sites), so neither accent has a fixed meaning.
findings.fix: Turn the slide 1 title bar into the deck's marker. Use a 64×6 amber rule to underline the one key fact on each slide: slide 2 under '99%' (12 px below the baseline, left-aligned to the '9'); slide 3 under the '2.4×' label; slide 4 under the 'uptime' label; slide 5 as a 6 px-wide amber tab at the left edge of the North row (x 64–70, full row height). Amber stays shape-only, because on white it is about 2:1 and cannot carry text. Blue stays as the data-highlight colour.

findings.element: region table and the empty right half
findings.problem: The table spans x 64–704, leaving the right 512 px empty. That is left-over space, not framing. The table proves 'North carries 17 of 41' only by reading numbers, with nothing to compare at a glance.
findings.fix: Widen the table to x 64–1088 and add an in-row bar column: Region text at x=80, a bar track at x 304–904 (bar height 16, vertically centred in the row, length = sites/17 × 600: North 600, Central 494, South 353). The North bar is blue #2E4BD8 and the others are blue at 25% tint. Right-align Sites at x=1072. The Total row has no bar. Keep the existing North row tint and the ink header rule.

findings.element: front card '20 sites / planned by Q1'
findings.problem: The card repeats the headline word for word ('20 more sites by Q1'), so the slide's most prominent object adds no information.
findings.fix: Change the card text to '41 → 61' (56 px/800 blue, real arrow U+2192, non-breaking spaces around it) with the label 'sites live by end of Q1' at 22 px ink. That states the destination and links to the slide 1 card.

findings.problem: The 88 px hero (slide 1) and 96 px stat (slide 4) are too close to read as different levels. Inter is used in 4 weights (400/600/700/800).
findings.fix: Set stats to 88 px so hero and stat share one step, or set the hero to 96 px. Replace the 600 weight (table header labels, footer wordmark) with 700 so the deck uses 400/700/800.

findings.element: subtitle 'A synthetic deck for a review-regression pilot. Every number in it is fictional.'
findings.problem: The greedy wrap leaves 'Every' stranded at the end of line 1 and splits the second sentence across lines.
findings.fix:
Break after 'pilot.': 'A synthetic deck for a review-regression pilot.
Every number in it is fictional.'

keep: Slide 3 native chart: direct value labels, no gridlines, Sep alone in full blue with Jul/Aug as clean blue tints
Slide 5 table craft: right-aligned numerals, tinted and bold North row, bold Total, single ink header rule
The consistent 64 px left margin, headline top (y≈123) on slides 3–5, and footer wordmark position on slides 2–6, so nothing jumps when advancing
Slide 1's optical alignment: the 88 px 'Q' is pulled left so its bowl lines up with the wordmark, amber bar and subtitle

The navy title slide alone on a dark ground, followed by white content slides

dismissed.reason: Deliberate optical side-bearing correction for the 88 px display 'Q' (design.md: nudge display caps left 2–4% of the font size). On screen, the Q aligns with 'Northstar Demo', the amber bar and the subtitle.

summary: Clean, on-brand and typographically careful, but not yet designed. Slide 6 breaks L1 (the card stack sits on the timeline), four headlines end in runts, and slides 3–5 leave a third to a half of the canvas as left-over space. Neither the card-stack motif nor amber has a job until the last slide. C1 and B1 are met.
